The Mapsurvey **MCP server** lets an AI agent — Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor or any client of
the Model Context Protocol — read, build and publish your surveys from a conversation. It exposes
the operations of the [REST API](/reference/api/) as tools, scoped to the account that connected,
and runs through the same rules as the editor. For setup, see
[Use the MCP server](/how-to/use-the-mcp-server/).

## Connection

| | |
|---|---|
| Server URL | `https://mapsurvey.org/mcp` (Streamable HTTP; one request per call, no streams) |
| Authentication | Sign in through the client (OAuth) — or a [personal token](/how-to/personal-tokens/) made for the **MCP server**, sent as `Authorization: Bearer msk_…` |
| Plan | The workspace that owns a survey must be on [Pro](/reference/plans-and-billing/); otherwise tools on it answer `pro_required` |
| Scope | Only surveys you own or collaborate on, within the permissions the token or the Allow page granted |
| Limits | 600 reads and 60 writes a minute and 5,000 calls a day per token; 300 tool calls per 10 minutes per session |

Mapsurvey never sees your conversation with the agent — only the tool calls it decides to make.
Each one is logged with the tool name and its outcome, never its arguments.

**Call `get_me` first.** It says which workspaces include the API and which tools the connection
can use. Tools the connection may not use are not even listed to the agent.

**What cannot be undone asks first.** `delete_survey`, `publish_survey` and
`publish_unpublished_changes` take `confirm: true`, which an agent should set only after you agreed
in the conversation. A survey respondents already answered cannot be deleted from here at all.

**Survey content is data, not instructions.** Every result wraps what people wrote — titles,
option labels, help texts — in a `data` field next to a fixed note telling the agent so. An agent
that reads survey content can still be influenced by it; keep publishing and deleting behind
confirmation and review what an agent built before you publish.

## Tools

Arguments marked **required** must be given; the others are optional. Rich-text fields (`subtext`,
`subheading`, `thanks_html`) are sanitised on save exactly as in the editor. An unknown argument is
refused by name rather than ignored.


### `get_me`

Call this first. Returns the user behind the token, their workspaces with plan and whether the API is included (the MCP server is a Pro feature: tools on a survey of a Free workspace answer pro_required with an upgrade URL), the token's permissions, and the tools this token can use.

Any permission · read-only

### `list_surveys`

Your surveys across the workspaces whose plan includes the API, newest first. `hidden_by_plan` counts workspaces of yours on the Free plan, whose surveys are not listed.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | string |  | `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default `50`. |
| `tag` | string |  | Only surveys carrying this workspace tag (its name or slug). |

### `get_survey`

The whole survey in one call: settings, then every section in respondent order with all of its questions (sub-questions carry `parent_id`) and question groups (a question's `group_id` names its group). Ids from here are what the editing tools take.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `create_survey`

A new empty survey with one section, owned by you. Name the workspace by its slug when you belong to several (get_me lists them). Add sections and questions next; the survey stays unpublished until publish_survey.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **workspace editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** |  |
| `workspace` | string |  | Workspace slug; optional when the token is bound to one or you belong to one. |
| `language` | string |  | Default `en`. |
| `map_start` | object (`lat`, `lng`, `zoom`) |  |  |

### `set_survey_tags`

Replace the survey's workspace tags, which group it with the datasets and other surveys of one engagement ("Riverside plan 2027"). Tags are created on first use and matched by slug; at most 10. Editor role.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tags` | list of string | **required** | The survey's new tags (replacing the old ones); created in the workspace on first use, matched by slug, at most 40 characters each. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `update_survey`

Change the fields you name: name, languages, redirect_url ("#" for the built-in thanks page), visibility, basemaps (preset keys or "style:<uuid>" of a workspace map style), branding, the thanks page per language, the map start, and the survey period (opens_at, closes_at, schedule_timezone: before opens_at respondents see an "opens on" page, at closes_at the survey closes by itself). Settings need the owner role; the thanks page the editor role.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **owner**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `redirect_url` | string |  | "#" for the built-in thanks page, or an absolute http(s) URL. |
| `languages` | list of string |  |  |
| `visibility` | `public` \| `private` \| `demo` |  |  |
| `basemaps` | list of string |  | Preset keys (streets, satellite, topo, paper, paper_b) or "style:<uuid>" of a workspace map style; a key the workspace does not have is dropped. |
| `default_basemap` | string |  | One of `basemaps`; else the first enabled key. |
| `show_branding` | boolean |  |  |
| `thanks_html` | map |  | Thanks page per language; creator HTML, sanitised on save. |
| `map_start` | object (`lat`, `lng`, `zoom`) |  |  |
| `use_geolocation` | boolean |  |  |
| `opens_at` | date-time |  | Start of the survey period: ISO 8601 with an offset, or a naive value read in schedule_timezone. Null clears it. |
| `closes_at` | date-time |  | End of the survey period, after the start and in the future. Null clears it. Reopening a survey by hand clears a past end. |
| `schedule_timezone` | string |  | IANA zone (e.g. "Europe/Berlin") naive period values are read in and times are shown in; "" = UTC. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `delete_survey`

Move a survey to the trash (the owner can restore it in the editor for 30 days). Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed. Refused when respondents have already answered: that deletion is done in the editor, where the answers are shown first. Unpublished changes are discarded with discard_unpublished_changes instead.

Permission `surveys:delete` · role **owner** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

### `publish_survey`

Make the survey live for respondents. Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed. `review: "pending"` in the result means content screening is holding it until a human looks; translation_gaps asks you to confirm publishing with missing translations.

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **owner** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acknowledge_translation_gaps` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |
| `clear_test_data` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

### `close_survey`

Stop collecting answers; the survey stays readable to its collaborators.

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **owner**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `start_unpublished_changes`

On a published or closed survey, structural edits (adding, deleting, reordering, changing a question type) answer draft_required. Call this to get an editable copy -- "unpublished changes" -- and edit the returned uuid; respondents keep the live survey until publish_unpublished_changes.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `publish_unpublished_changes`

Replace the live survey with its unpublished changes as a new version. Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed. incompatible_draft means the changes conflict with collected answers; repeat with `force: true` only if the user accepts that.

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **owner** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acknowledge_translation_gaps` | boolean |  | Default `False`. |
| `force` | boolean |  | Publish even when the changes conflict with collected answers. Default `False`. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

### `discard_unpublished_changes`

Throw the unpublished changes away; the live survey is untouched.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **owner** · cannot be undone

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys or create_survey). |

### `create_section`

Append a section (a page) to the survey; the other fields set it at once. `layout` is "map" (the page shows the map, for geo questions), "image" (a picture beside the questions, e.g. a welcome page; the picture is uploaded in the editor, else the survey cover is shown) or "form". `panel_side` (left|right) and `panel_width` (default|third|half) place the questions on a computer screen; `content_width` (full|column) and `content_valign` (top|middle) place the content inside that panel; `keep_panel_open` keeps the questions visible while respondents place on the map (desktop, map sections). On a live survey this is a structural change: start_unpublished_changes first.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `subheading` | string |  |  |
| `code` | string |  |  |
| `layout` | `map` \| `image` \| `form` |  |  |
| `panel_side` | `left` \| `right` |  |  |
| `panel_width` | `default` \| `third` \| `half` |  |  |
| `content_width` | `full` \| `column` |  |  |
| `content_valign` | `top` \| `middle` |  |  |
| `keep_panel_open` | boolean |  |  |
| `next_label` | string |  |  |
| `visibility_rule` | object (`question_code`, `choice_codes`, `answered`) |  |  |
| `audience` | `everyone` \| `respondents` \| `operators` |  | Who sees it: everyone, respondents only, or operators only (the "Enter a response" form workspace members fill in for someone else). Changing it on a live survey needs unpublished changes. |
| `translations` | map |  |  |
| `map_start` | object (`lat`, `lng`, `zoom`) |  |  |
| `use_geolocation` | boolean |  |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

### `add_question`

Add a question at the end of a section. `input_type` picks the kind: text, text_line, number, choice, multichoice (with `choices`), range, rating, datetime, image, html (a formatted text block), and the map types point, line, polygon, spraycan. With `parent_question_id` (a geo or Objects question) it becomes a sub-question asked in that question's pop-up for every placed feature -- the only way to attach attributes to what respondents draw. `subtext` is help text (creator HTML, sanitised on save). On a live survey this is a structural change: start_unpublished_changes first.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `subtext` | string |  |  |
| `input_type` | `text` \| `number` \| `choice` \| `multichoice` \| `range` \| `rating` \| `ranking` \| `datetime` \| `point` \| `line` \| `polygon` \| `spraycan` \| `image` \| `text_line` \| `html` \| `photo` \| `audio` \| `document` \| `thumbs` \| `layer_objects` \| `budget` | **required** |  |
| `required` | boolean |  |  |
| `choices` | list of object (`code`, `name`, `other`, `icon`, `group`, `color`, `description`, `cost`) |  |  |
| `validation_settings` | object (`min_value`, `max_value`, `max_dots`, `max_file_mb`, `max_files`, `min_features`, `max_features`) |  |  |
| `budget` | object (`mode`, `total`, `unit`, `symbol`, `step`, `rule`, `min_items`, `show_shares`, `source`, `cost_property`) |  | Settings of a `budget` question. |
| `price` | object (`amount`, `per`) |  | A map question's price under a budget group; null removes it. |
| `color` | string |  |  |
| `icon_class` | string |  |  |
| `display_style` | string |  |  |
| `visibility_rule` | object (`question_code`, `choice_codes`, `answered`) |  |  |
| `audience` | `everyone` \| `respondents` \| `operators` |  | Who sees it: everyone, respondents only, or operators only (the "Enter a response" form workspace members fill in for someone else). Changing it on a live survey needs unpublished changes. |
| `layer_id` | integer |  |  |
| `layer_from_answers` | string |  | For an "Objects on the map" question: the code of a map question whose answers become a shared map (created on first use). Use instead of `layer_id`. |
| `min_objects` | integer |  |  |
| `share_with_respondents` | boolean |  |  |
| `translations` | map |  |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `section_id` | integer | **required** | The section id (from get_survey). |
| `parent_question_id` | integer |  | Make it a sub-question of this geo / Objects question (same section). |

### `delete_question`

Delete a question with its sub-questions. Answers go too: the first call answers answers_at_risk with the count; repeat with `acknowledge_answer_loss: true` only after the user agreed.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor** · cannot be undone

### `reorder_questions`

Renumber a section's top-level questions (or one pop-up's sub-questions, with `parent_id`). `items` are question ids in the new order; a question group is `{"g": <group id>, "q": [<ids>]}`.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parent_id` | integer |  | Order a pop-up's sub-questions instead of the section's top level. |
| `items` | list of integer or map | **required** | Question ids in order; a group is {"g": <id>, "q": [<ids>]}. |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `section_id` | integer | **required** | The section id (from get_survey). |

### `set_choices`

Replace the options of a choice / multichoice question. Keep an option's `code` to keep its answers; a new option gets a code never used in the survey's history. `name` is a string or a {language: text} map.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `choices` | list of object (`code`, `name`, `other`, `icon`, `group`, `color`, `description`, `cost`) | **required** |  |
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid. |
| `question_id` | integer | **required** | The question id (from get_survey). |

### `import_survey`

Create a whole survey from one document: the `survey.json` of Mapsurvey's backup format (version "1.0", a `survey` object with `name`, `available_languages`, `sections` with `questions`). The import runs in the background; the result is a job -- poll get_import_job until its status is done or failed. Name the workspace by its slug when you belong to several.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **workspace editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_json` | map | **required** | The survey.json document as an object, not a string. |
| `workspace` | string |  | Workspace slug. |

### `get_import_job`

One of your import jobs: status (queued, running, done, failed), the survey it made, warnings.

Permission `surveys:read` · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | integer | **required** | The job id import_survey returned. |

### `get_response_summary`

How many responses a survey has and what they say, question by question in section order: option counts with the most frequent "other" write-ins, number statistics, rating means, text and map answer counts. Sub-questions of map questions are nested under their map question; "Objects on the map" questions list each object with its answers. Counts the responses an export contains: no empty, deleted or rejected ones unless include_all. Start a report here, then use list_text_answers and get_answer_geojson for detail.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `version` | string |  | One version (v3), several separated by commas (v10,v11), or omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted, on-hold and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that answered every required question. Default `False`. |

### `list_responses`

Individual responses, newest first, each with its "#N" number, language, validation status and every answer (map answers as GeoJSON geometry with their sub-answers). Prefer get_response_summary for numbers; use this to read particular responses.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `include_empty` | boolean |  | Also responses that answered nothing. Default `False`. |
| `cursor` | string |  | `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default `20`. |

### `list_text_answers`

The non-blank answers to one text question or text sub-question, newest first, each with the response number. Page through with `next_cursor` to read every comment.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |

| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that answered every required question. Default `False`. |
| `cursor` | string |  | `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default `50`. |

### `get_answer_geojson`

The points, lines, areas or spray clouds respondents drew for one map question, as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (WGS 84). Each feature carries the answers to the sub-questions as properties and the response it came from. Stops at `limit` features and then says `truncated: true`; for everything, hand the person a link from get_export_link.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `question_id` | integer | **required** | A question id from get_survey. |
| `version` | string |  | One version (v3), several separated by commas (v10,v11), or omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted, on-hold and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that answered every required question. Default `False`. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most features to return. Default `200`. |

### `get_export_link`

A link for the person to download the responses as a file -- xlsx (Excel), csv, zip (GeoJSON + CSV), gpkg (GeoPackage), shp (Shapefile) or kml. It works for 15 minutes and checks access again when opened. Give the person the link; do not try to open it yourself.

Permission `responses:read` · role **viewer** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `format` | `xlsx` \| `csv` \| `zip` \| `gpkg` \| `shp` \| `kml` |  | Default `xlsx`. |
| `version` | string |  | One version (v3), several separated by commas (v10,v11), or omit for every version. |
| `include_all` | boolean |  | Also count deleted, on-hold and rejected responses. Default `False`. |
| `completed_only` | boolean |  | Only responses that answered every required question. Default `False`. |
| `files` | boolean |  | Add files respondents uploaded. Default `False`. |

### `moderate_response`

Set a response's status: approved, on_hold, not_approved (held and rejected responses leave exports, summaries and public results), or "" to clear it. It can be changed back. Needs the editor role.

Permission `responses:moderate` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |

### `create_dataset_view`

A named view of a dataset. On a layer: conditions on public fields (eq, in, gt, lt) and the fields it keeps. On the answers to a map question: kind grid (respondents per cell), coverage (lines and areas: share of respondents per cell) or density (points and spray: marks per cell). On a survey's responses: kind engagement (opened, answered, finished) or crosstab (config.rows and config.columns are the codes of two choice questions). Small groups are always hidden. Read a computed view with get_dataset_view_data.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** |  |
| `kind` | `objects` \| `grid` \| `coverage` \| `density` \| `engagement` \| `crosstab` |  | What the view yields; left out, the dataset's default. A layer takes `objects`; the answers to a map question take `grid`, plus `coverage` (lines, areas) or `density` (points, spray); a survey's responses take `engagement` and `crosstab`. |
| `config` | object (`rows`, `columns`) |  | Settings of the kind: the two questions of a cross-tab. |
| `color` | string |  | #rrggbb |
| `conditions` | list of object (`field`, `op`, `value`, `values`) |  | All must hold. Layer datasets only; collected answers are a grid. |
| `fields` | list of string |  | Public fields the view keeps; empty = all. |
| `dataset_id` | integer | **required** | A dataset id from list_datasets. |

### `get_dataset_view_data`

What an engagement, crosstab, grid, coverage or density view yields. Every count under the privacy threshold K comes back masked (value null, display "<K") and map cells with fewer than K respondents are left out — for every caller.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **workspace member** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset_id` | integer | **required** | A dataset id from list_datasets. |
| `view_id` | integer | **required** | A view id from get_dataset. |

### `upload_dataset_version`

A new file for a layer dataset, matched row by row on its key field. The job stops at preview with added, changed, removed and unchanged counts — nothing is saved until apply_dataset_version.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset_id` | integer | **required** | A dataset id from list_datasets. |
| `filename` | string | **required** | The file name with its extension: .geojson, .json, .csv, .kml, .gpkg or .zip (a shapefile). |
| `content` | string |  | The file as text (GeoJSON, CSV, KML). |
| `content_base64` | string |  | The file as base64 (GeoPackage, zipped shapefile, or any text format). |

### `apply_dataset_version`

Apply a previewed version with a note. Objects whose key stays are updated in place and keep their answers; every survey and site that shows the dataset shows the new version.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `job_id` | integer | **required** | The version job id. |
| `note` | string |  | What changed. |

### `link_dataset`

Add a public layer dataset (or one of its views) to a survey's reference layers — linked, not copied, so an edit of the dataset shows on the survey. Up to 5,000 objects and 10 layers per survey. Owner role.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **owner**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `dataset_id` | integer | **required** | A dataset id from list_datasets. |
| `view_id` | integer |  | A view id from get_dataset. |

### `unlink_dataset`

Remove a linked dataset from a survey's reference layers; refused while a question of the survey shows it. Owner role.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **owner**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey` | uuid | **required** | The survey uuid (from list_surveys). |
| `link_id` | integer | **required** | The link id link_dataset returned. |

### `list_reports`

The reports of a workspace you may see: title, home survey, whether each is published, its address, tags and when it last changed. Filter by a tag.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **workspace member** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string |  | Workspace slug; needed when you belong to several. |
| `tag` | string |  | A workspace tag, by name or slug. |

### `get_report`

One report: its title and opening paragraph, settings, how often it was read, and every block in order with its id — the ids feed update_report_block and reorder_report_blocks.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **workspace member** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |

### `create_report`

A new report, never published on creation. With `template` (summary, council, update, yousaid) it is drafted from the survey's answers by rules: who took part, a block per answered question, and candidate quotes as a hidden block for a person to pick from. Without it the report is empty. Reports are part of Pro.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace` | string |  | Workspace slug; needed when you belong to several. |
| `survey` | uuid |  | The home survey. With `template`, the survey the draft is made from. |
| `template` | `summary` \| `council` \| `update` \| `yousaid` |  | Draft the report from the survey's answers by rules: summary, council paper, engagement update, you said — we did. Left out: an empty report. |
| `title` | string |  |  |

### `update_report`

Change a report's title, the line above it, the opening paragraph, the privacy threshold K (groups smaller than K are hidden; lowering it shows smaller groups of people), its tags or the sites that may embed it. Only the fields you send change.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string |  |  |
| `eyebrow` | string |  | The line above the title. |
| `lead` | string |  | The opening paragraph; tokens are filled. |
| `k` | integer |  | Groups smaller than K are hidden. 1 hides nothing. |
| `tags` | list of string |  |  |
| `embed_hosts` | list of string |  | Sites that may embed the report; empty = any. |
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |

### `add_report_block`

Add a block at the end of a report. Written by you: heading (`text`), text (`html`, may hold tokens {responses} {opened} {finished} {marks:CODE} {respondents:CODE} that are filled from the home survey), numbers (`items` of value + label), quotes (`items` of text + source — publish a quote only when the person asked for it). Shown from answers: chart, map, objects or budget of one `question` code; crosstab of `rows` and `columns` question codes; engagement; compare of one `question` code with the same code in an `other` survey (two rounds side by side). Small groups are hidden in every data block. `show_marks` on a map shows individual marks, which can point at someone's home: off unless the person asks. A map is drawn as `view` heat, hotspots (point questions only), squares or marks (needs `show_marks`), with the view's `opts` (send the whole set), `color`, `name`, a kept `frame` [west, south, east, north] (null clears it), `legend`, `scale`, `toggle`, `study_area` (the survey's study area outline, on by default), `basemap` and `popup_fields`; `layers` are up to 3 other map questions drawn on the same map — always the whole list: read it from get_report, change it, send it back (ids are kept). A layer's `show_marks` is off unless the person asks. A crosstab's look is `display` {view: bars | stacked | ranking | table, values: percent | count, sort}.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `heading` \| `text` \| `numbers` \| `quotes` \| `chart` \| `map` \| `objects` \| `budget` \| `crosstab` \| `engagement` \| `compare` | **required** |  |
| `title` | string |  | A title above the block. |
| `width` | `full` \| `half` |  | Two half-width blocks in a row sit side by side. |
| `hidden` | boolean |  | Kept in the report, not shown on its page. |
| `text` | string |  | heading: the heading. |
| `html` | string |  | text: rich text (sanitised). Tokens {responses}, {opened}, {finished}, {marks:CODE}, {respondents:CODE} are filled from the home survey. |
| `items` | list of object (`value`, `label`, `text`, `source`) |  | numbers: value + label; quotes: text + source. |
| `note` | string |  | numbers: a line under them. |
| `survey` | uuid |  | The survey a data block shows; default: the report's home survey. |
| `question` | string |  | chart / map / objects / budget / compare: the question code. |
| `other` | uuid |  | compare: the other survey (another round) that has a question with the same code. |
| `viz` | `auto` \| `bar` \| `pie` \| `donut` \| `table` |  | chart: how it is drawn. |
| `rows` | string |  | crosstab: the code of the question in the rows. |
| `columns` | string |  | crosstab: the code of the question in the columns. |
| `show_marks` | boolean |  | map: the marks themselves instead of squares that count respondents. A mark can point at someone's home. |
| `style` | `list` \| `pull` \| `cards` |  | quotes: one under another (list), each large (pull), or two columns (cards). |
| `description` | string |  | map: what it shows, in a sentence (also read by screen readers). |
| `view` | `heat` \| `hotspots` \| `squares` \| `marks` |  | map: heat (soft shading), hotspots (numbered places, point questions only), squares (cells that count respondents) or marks (every mark; needs show_marks). |
| `opts` | object (`spread`, `strength`, `top`, `place`, `list`, `shade`, `cell`, `size`, `solid`) |  | map: the view's settings — the whole set. |
| `color` | string |  | map: the colour of its own question, #rrggbb. |
| `name` | string |  | map: the name of its own question in the legend. |
| `frame` | list of number |  | map: the part kept in view, [west, south, east, north] in degrees; null clears it (the whole of the answers). |
| `legend` | boolean |  | map: the legend (on by default). |
| `scale` | boolean |  | map: the scale bar (on by default). |
| `toggle` | boolean |  | map: readers may switch layers on and off. |
| `study_area` | boolean |  | map: the outline of the survey's study area (on by default). |
| `basemap` | string |  | map: a basemap key the workspace offers. |
| `popup_fields` | list of string |  | map: codes of sub-questions a popup shows (never free text). |
| `layers` | list of object (`id`, `survey`, `question`, `view`, `show_marks`, `color`, `name`, `opts`, `popup_fields`) |  | map: the other map questions on the same map — the whole list, at most 3; [] removes them. |
| `display` | object (`view`, `values`, `sort`) |  | crosstab: how it is drawn. |
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |

### `update_report_block`

Change a block's text, items, title, width (full or half — two halves in a row sit side by side) or whether it is hidden. Its type and its question stay: to show another question, add another block. Settings left out stay as they are. A map is drawn as `view` heat, hotspots (point questions only), squares or marks (needs `show_marks`), with the view's `opts` (send the whole set), `color`, `name`, a kept `frame` [west, south, east, north] (null clears it), `legend`, `scale`, `toggle`, `study_area` (the survey's study area outline, on by default), `basemap` and `popup_fields`; `layers` are up to 3 other map questions drawn on the same map — always the whole list: read it from get_report, change it, send it back (ids are kept). A layer's `show_marks` is off unless the person asks. A crosstab's look is `display` {view: bars | stacked | ranking | table, values: percent | count, sort}.

| `view` | `heat` \| `hotspots` \| `squares` \| `marks` |  | map: heat (soft shading), hotspots (numbered places, point questions only), squares (cells that count respondents) or marks (every mark; needs show_marks). |
| `opts` | object (`spread`, `strength`, `top`, `place`, `list`, `shade`, `cell`, `size`, `solid`) |  | map: the view's settings — the whole set. |

| `frame` | list of number |  | map: the part kept in view, [west, south, east, north] in degrees; null clears it (the whole of the answers). |

Remove one block from a report. The answers it showed are not touched.

Put a report's blocks in a new order: every block id of the report, once.

### `get_report_checks`

What to look at before a report is published: under `people`, every quote written out and every map that shows individual marks; under `unfinished`, empty blocks, maps without a description, hidden blocks. Read `people` to the user before publish_report when `needs_confirm` is true.

Permission `surveys:read` · role **workspace member** · read-only

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |

### `publish_report`

Publish a report at its address, or take it down with `publish: false`. `visibility`: public (search engines may list it), unlisted (anyone with the link), workspace (signed-in members). `mode`: live follows new answers, frozen keeps the numbers of now. A report that shows quotes or individual marks needs `confirm: true` after the user read them (get_report_checks).

Permission `surveys:publish` · role **editor** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `publish` | boolean |  | Default `True`. |
| `visibility` | `public` \| `unlisted` \| `workspace` |  |  |
| `mode` | `live` \| `frozen` |  | live follows new answers; frozen keeps the numbers of now. |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Required to publish a report that shows quotes or individual marks: the person confirmed having read them. Default `False`. |
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |

### `freeze_report`

Freeze a report's numbers as they are now ("Data as of …"), or with `frozen: false` return it to numbers that follow new answers.

Permission `surveys:write` · role **editor**

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frozen` | boolean |  | Default `True`. |
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |

### `delete_report`

Delete a report with its blocks and pictures; its address stops working. The survey and its answers are not touched. Needs `confirm: true` after the user agreed; it cannot be undone.

Permission `surveys:delete` · role **editor** · needs `confirm: true`

| Argument | Type | | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `report` | uuid | **required** | The report uuid (from list_reports). |
| `confirm` | boolean |  | Set to true only after the user confirmed this action in the conversation. Default `False`. |

## Errors

A refused call comes back as a tool error carrying the same envelope as the REST API:
`{"error": "<code>", "detail": "<text>", ...}`.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `scope_missing` | The connection lacks the permission this tool needs (`scope` names it). |
| `pro_required` | The survey's workspace is not on Pro (`upgrade_url` links to its billing page). |
| `forbidden_role` | You can see the survey but your role on it is too low (`role` names the one needed). |
| `not_found` | Nothing there — or nothing you may see. The two are deliberately the same answer. |
| `validation` | An argument is invalid for this survey; `fields` lists what and why. |
| `draft_required` | A structural change to a live survey: call `start_unpublished_changes` and edit the returned uuid (`draft` is it when it already exists). |
| `answers_at_risk` | The delete would remove `count` answers; repeat with `acknowledge_answer_loss: true` after the user agreed. |
| `delete_blocked` | Something else depends on what you are deleting. |
| `translation_gaps` | Some languages are missing text; repeat with `acknowledge_translation_gaps: true`. |
| `incompatible_draft` | Unpublished changes conflict with collected answers; repeat with `force: true` only if the user accepts that. |
| `transition_refused` | The survey cannot move to that status from where it is. |
| `conflict` | The request conflicts with the current state (e.g. unpublished changes already exist). |
| `confirmation_required` | An irreversible tool was called without `confirm: true`. |
| `has_responses` | The survey has `count` answered responses; delete it in the editor instead. |
| `rate_limited` | Too many calls; wait `retry_after` seconds (`limit` names the window). |
| `server_error` | Our fault. It is logged; retrying a read later is safe. |

A malformed request — an unknown tool, or arguments that do not fit the schema — is a protocol
error (`-32602`) naming the fields; a missing or invalid token is HTTP `401`; a request from an
unexpected browser origin is `403`.
